name: Saddamism
summary: Saddamism is the Ba'thist ideology of Saddam Hussein and of Iraq under his rule (1979-2003): pan-Arab nationalism centred on Iraq, rule by a single party fused with a personality cult around the leader, a state-led socialist economy built on nationalised oil that admitted a regulated private sector and was partly liberalised from 1987, and an anti-imperialist, anti-Zionist foreign policy. Secular into the 1980s, it turned to a state-promoted Islam with the Faith Campaign of 1993, and its record includes wars on Iran and Kuwait, the Anfal campaign against the Kurds and systematic repression of opponents.
scope: Saddam Hussein's political thought and the practice of the Iraqi state and Ba'th Party he led, as Malhotra (s6) and Baram (s7, s8) define it: his speeches, interviews and writings from the 1970s to 2001 (s1, s23-s40), the party's Ninth Regional Congress report of 1982, which presents his ideas as its guidelines (s19), and the regime's record from 1979 to 2003 as reported by the Library of Congress, Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International (s9-s18). Policies of the 1968-79 period are included where Saddam drove them as deputy (oil nationalisation, the 1970 constitution and land reform). It excludes the Syrian Ba'th, Aflaq's thought as such, and post-2003 Ba'thist insurgent groups.

notes: Later pass (rules 5) by claude-opus-5-5. The first pass rested on Wikipedia and on sources about Ba'thism in general; this pass rebuilt it from Saddam's own speeches and writings (archive.org copies of the Baghdad translations, 1974-2001), the 1982 Ninth Regional Congress report, the 1970 constitution, and the regime's record as reported by the Library of Congress country study (1988), Human Rights Watch (1992-2004) and Amnesty International (2001), with Baram's study of the regime and religion and Malhotra's article on the term. Record over words: where the regime acted (elections, courts, media, land reform, wars, Arabization, the Faith Campaign) the answer rests on the record alone. Over time: the economy was state-led socialism from 1968 with a partial liberalisation from 1987, and religion turned from secular rule to the 1993-2003 Faith Campaign, an explicit change sustained for a decade, which the religion answers follow. Every first-pass answer was rechecked; those the new sources do not settle are nulled. Blocked: the Washington Institute (s5), the US State Department human rights reports, refworld, FPRI and DTIC refused scripted access, and Bengio's Saddam's Word, Sassoon's Saddam Hussein's Ba'th Party and Saddam's On Social and Foreign Affairs in Iraq were available only as lending copies. Themes searched: economy (planning, property, land reform, wages, unions, prices, oil, foreign capital), government (party, elections, RCC, courts, presidency, autonomy), society (women, education, religion, minorities, Arabization), liberty (media, internet, death penalty, torture, punishments), world (wars, the UN, Palestine, non-alignment, Arab unity, nuclear programme). Ecology, technology and most questions of social policy stay null: the sources say nothing on them.
